data.narrative:
MightyFly is a Series A-stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Manal Habib that has raised $10M to date. The target sector includes eight private peers (Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and others) and no directly comparable public companies, limiting traditional public market benchmarking.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $10M total raised as a proxy for post-seed value, implying a $20M valuation. The peer-median approach was not applicable; while seven same-sector peers exist in the Drones & Autonomous universe, none satisfied the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparability (fewer than three datapoints in any narrow category). A broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of autonomous systems applications and development timelines.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $17M–$23M, centered at $20M, based on the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow peer transaction data for Series A drone companies, which limits confidence in the 2.0x multiplier's appropriateness for MightyFly's specific risk and market conditions. A richer peer dataset at identical stage and technology focus would substantially improve precision. Current range reflects method-agnostic bounds rather than high-confidence triangulation across independent approaches.
